section_summary: This section finishes a series of Japanese general licenses governing transactions with designated foreigners, then reproduces the Enemy Assets Control Law and its implementing ordinance and regulations. A finance overview and a detailed account of the revised Bank of Japan law describe the wartime expansion of state control over banking. The section ends with the revised Foreign Exchange Control Law and the opening chapters of its enforcement regulations, which continue beyond page 519.

subfiles.title: General license concerning transactions with designated foreigners, concluding text
subfiles.about: Concludes an earlier license concerning bank transactions involving designated foreigners.
subfiles.summary: The concluding provision defines nationals of designated foreign countries by reference to Ministry of Finance notifications.

subfiles.title: Notification No. 290: General License No. 2
subfiles.about: Permits specified clearing transactions involving bills accepted before July 28, 1941.
subfiles.summary: The license covers clearing between banks and related transactions involving banks or customers classified as designated foreigners.

subfiles.title: Notification No. 293: General License No. 3
subfiles.about: Permits specified clearing transactions involving bills accepted before July 29, 1941.
subfiles.summary: The license lists permitted dealings among banks and designated foreigners for bills cleared on July 30.

subfiles.title: Notification No. 300: General License No. 4
subfiles.about: Allows limited withdrawals from designated-country nationals’ deposits until August 15, 1941.
subfiles.summary: Withdrawals may pay Japanese taxes, public dues, or wages to Japanese workers in Japan.

subfiles.title: Notification No. 301: General License No. 5
subfiles.about: Exempts transactions conducted by government offices.
subfiles.summary: The license designates acts conducted by government offices as permitted.

subfiles.title: Notification No. 302: General License No. 6
subfiles.about: Permits specified debt repayments, deposits, and related currency transactions.
subfiles.summary: The license permits designated-country nationals and eligible banks to settle debts and deposits, subject in some cases to the Japanese counterparty’s permission.

subfiles.title: Notification No. 303: General License No. 7
subfiles.about: Exempts specified payments and purchases of drafts from individual permission.
subfiles.summary: The license covers drafts tied to letters of credit and certain Japanese bank transactions, including cases where earlier permissions have become invalid.

subfiles.title: Notification No. 305: General License No. 8
subfiles.about: Permits specified clearing transactions involving bills accepted before July 31, 1941.
subfiles.summary: The license covers August 1 clearing and associated dealings involving banks classified as designated foreigners.

subfiles.title: Notification No. 310: General License No. 9
subfiles.about: Permits specified clearing transactions involving bills accepted before August 1, 1941.
subfiles.summary: The license covers August 2 clearing and related dealings involving banks classified as designated foreigners.

subfiles.title: Notification No. 311: General License No. 10
subfiles.about: Permits transfer of specified movable property from designated foreigners to Japanese recipients.
subfiles.summary: The permitted transfer must be based on a freight receipt prepared within the regulations’ area of application.

subfiles.title: Notification No. 312: General License No. 11
subfiles.about: Permits designated foreigners to make specified routine financial payments.
subfiles.summary: The license covers bank, trust, insurance, and warehouse charges, along with interest, dividends, premiums, freight, and safekeeping fees.

subfiles.title: Notification No. 313: General License No. 12
subfiles.about: Permits specified deposits, loans, and trusts involving designated foreigners.
subfiles.summary: The license allows transactions with eligible banks and trust companies; some dealings with Japanese persons require the Japanese counterparty’s permission.

subfiles.title: Enemy Assets Control Law in Japan, Law No. 99
subfiles.about: Establishes government administration and control of enemy assets.
subfiles.summary: The law authorizes administrators, restricts enemy owners’ dealings, governs debts and overseas transactions involving Japanese assets, and imposes penalties for evasion. It also establishes an Enemy Assets Control Committee.

subfiles.title: Ordinance Relative to the Application of the Enemy Assets Control Law of Japan, Imperial Ordinance No. 1179
subfiles.about: Defines enemy nationals and sets procedures for administering enemy assets.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance defines covered persons, provides for appointment and duties of asset administrators, and governs registration, sale, approval, and remuneration. It assigns corresponding ministerial authority in Chosen, Taiwan, and Karafuto.

subfiles.title: Regulations Relative to the Application of the Enemy Assets Control Law in Japan, Ministry of Finance Order No. 76
subfiles.about: Specifies procedures and reporting requirements for administering enemy assets.
subfiles.summary: The order requires handover, inventories, quarterly reports, account books, and applications for approval of overseas dealings. The translated forms are omitted.

subfiles.title: VIII. Finance: Introductory Note
subfiles.about: Introduces Japanese banking, foreign exchange control, and taxation.
subfiles.summary: The note describes special and ordinary financial institutions, the Bank of Japan’s central role, the development of exchange controls, and income tax revenue during the war.

subfiles.title: Summary of Revised Law of the Bank of Japan Indicating Differences from the Original Law
subfiles.about: Compares the revised Bank of Japan law with the earlier law.
subfiles.summary: The article-by-article account covers the bank’s status, personnel, business powers, note issue, accounting, ministerial supervision, and penalties. It emphasizes broader authority over credit and foreign exchange, stronger government appointments and oversight, and the transfer of most remaining profits to the state.

subfiles.title: Revised Foreign Exchange Control Law of Japan, Law No. 83 of 1941
subfiles.about: Authorizes broad controls over foreign exchange, payments, securities, and overseas property.
subfiles.summary: The law empowers the government to restrict transactions, direct sales of foreign assets, prescribe international settlement methods, and require reports and inspections. It provides criminal penalties and establishes a Foreign Exchange Control Commission.

subfiles.title: Enforcement Regulations of the Foreign Exchange Control Law of Japan, Finance Ministry Ordinance No. 10
subfiles.about: Sets permit, reporting, and exemption rules under the Foreign Exchange Control Law.
subfiles.summary: The regulations define exchange instruments, securities, property, and residency, then govern currency dealing, letters of credit, remittances, gold, collections, and travelers’ funds. Later chapters address foreign-currency securities, overseas credits and obligations, guarantees, and acquisition of foreign property. The text continues beyond page 519.
